question: Marvell-inspired network. The notice affects TW_air only. A planner who reads it as affecting every air lane plans for TW_air and MY_air. When does that reading change dispatch decisions, and what does it cost once the plan meets what occurs?
source_case: benchmarks/planning_agent_v2/cases.json A04; disruption arguments as the model sent them in benchmark_results/planning_agent_v2_1/a04_retest/runs.jsonl

varied.reason: Taiwan and Malaysia cargo share no lane. The only lane that can carry the cargo MY_air carries is MY_road, so its weekly space decides whether MY_air is needed in weeks 7-9. Demand, service terms and every other input stay fixed.
varied.unit: multiple of mean weekly Malaysia demand in kg, as in network_planning/config.json

reveal_note: The planner learns the true scope at the start of this week. Earlier dispatches and the season's air reservation stay as planned. 1: only the reservation is committed; 7: learns when the window opens; 10: learns after the window. The plan carried out with no re-planning at all is evaluated as well.
decided_before_running: Grid, reveal weeks, tolerance and tie-break weight were fixed after solving only the original case (ratio 1.5), where both readings give the same plan. Zero-regret and infeasible results are kept.
